A portable stand (10) comprises a back wall (12), a base element (14), and two opposed end plates (16), between which the back wall and the base element extend to define an open-topped, box-like container. The stand further comprises legs (35) that can be folded adjacent to the base element (14), and support arms (40), each having a pivotal connection (42) that allows it to move between a closed position adjacent to the back wall (12) and a second position projecting upward from the back wall (12).

The stand additionally comprises a front panel (20), hinged to the base element (14), that can be swung between a position in which it forms a front wall of the box-like container and a position in which it extends below the base element (14). A top panel (22), hinged to the back wall (12), can similarly be swung between a position in which it forms a lid for the box-like container and a position in which it extends above the back wall (12).

Swinging the front panel (20) and the top panel (22) in this manner opens the box-like container and exposes the display surfaces of both panels. The container may include multiple display chambers (66), which are also revealed when the panels are opened. The portable stand thereby enables information to be presented on the exposed surfaces and items to be exhibited within the display chambers (66), for example, for safety purposes.

A transportable stand (10) includes a rear wall (12) and a bottom member (14), both extending between a pair of opposing end plates (16) to form a box-shaped receptacle with an open upper side. Foldable legs (35) can be stored alongside the bottom member (14). The stand also has support arms (40), each mounted by a pivot joint (42), allowing movement from a stowed position beside the rear wall (12) to a raised position projecting above it.

A front panel (20) is pivotally attached to the bottom member (14) and can move between an upright position, in which it serves as the receptacle’s front wall, and a lowered position beneath the bottom member (14). Similarly, a top panel (22) is hinged to the rear wall (12) and is movable between a closed position, where it acts as a lid, and an elevated position above the rear wall (12). Moving both panels to their extended positions opens the receptacle and reveals the outward-facing surfaces of the front and top panels (20, 22). The receptacle may contain several display compartments (66), which are also exposed when it is opened. Information can be presented on the revealed panel surfaces, while objects may be exhibited in the compartments (66), including for safety-related applications.
outputs.L3:
The portable stand is designed as an open-top, box-like container comprising a back wall, a base element, and two opposed end plates. This compact structure provides an enclosure for storing and displaying materials while remaining easy to transport.

Foldable legs are attached to the stand and can be positioned adjacent to the base element when not in use, creating a compact configuration for storage and portability. When deployed, the legs support the stand at a convenient height. Pivoting support arms are also provided and can move between a closed position, in which they rest against the back wall, and an open position, in which they project upward to support the stand’s display components.

Hinged front and top panels open outward from the container. In their open positions, these panels expose display surfaces while also providing access to the interior of the stand. Information, instructions, notices, or promotional content may be presented on the panels, while internal display chambers can hold relevant objects or materials. The stand is particularly suitable for presenting safety-related information and equipment, although it may also be adapted for educational, informational, or commercial displays.
outputs.L4:
The portable display stand is designed to function both as a compact carrying container and as an upright presentation unit. In its closed configuration, the stand has the general form of an open-top, box-like container that can hold display materials, safety equipment, literature, or other items during storage and transport. Foldable legs, movable support components, and hinged panels are arranged against or within the container so that the unit occupies relatively little space and can be carried conveniently between locations.

To erect the stand, the foldable legs are moved outward and downward from their stored positions to support the container at a suitable viewing height. Pivoting support arms are then extended to stabilize the legs and maintain the stand in its open, upright configuration. The support arms may also help position and retain the display panels, reducing the likelihood that the stand will collapse or close unintentionally during use.

A front panel is connected to the body of the stand by one or more hinges. When the unit is opened, this panel pivots away from the container to expose an information-bearing surface. A hinged top panel can likewise be raised or repositioned to provide an additional display area. The front and top panels may carry printed instructions, notices, diagrams, branding, warnings, emergency procedures, or other visual information appropriate to the intended application.

One or more optional display chambers may be provided within the body of the stand. These chambers can store and present articles such as personal protective equipment, emergency supplies, product samples, tools, brochures, or demonstration materials. Opening the front or top panels makes the chamber contents visible and accessible while also revealing the informational surfaces associated with the panels. Transparent covers, retainers, shelves, or dividers may be used to organize and protect the displayed items.

After use, the panels can be folded back toward the body, the support arms released and pivoted into their storage positions, and the legs folded against or beneath the container. The displayed articles may remain inside the chambers for transport, allowing the entire assembly to be moved as a single compact unit.

This convertible construction provides a practical portable display that can be stored and transported like a container but quickly deployed as a stable, elevated presentation station. It is particularly useful for displaying safety information and related equipment, although it may also be adapted for exhibitions, training sessions, demonstrations, retail presentations, public-information events, and other temporary display applications.

The old wooden swing hung beneath the oak tree, moving gently in the evening breeze. There, beyond the garden fence, the sun slipped below the hills and painted the sky in shades of gold. The rhythmic creak of the ropes carried memories of childhood summers, when every push felt like flying. Swinging higher, the world seemed wider, lighter, and full of possibility.

## Collapsible Exhibition Stand

A portable, self-contained display unit designed for exhibitions, retail presentations, and temporary information points. In transport mode, the stand forms a compact, enclosed cabinet that protects printed materials, equipment, and display components.

For deployment, the hinged front panel folds downward to expose internal storage compartments and create a stable access shelf or presentation surface. The top panel swings upward on concealed hinges, revealing an additional information surface suitable for graphics, instructions, branding, or interchangeable display media. Integrated stays or locking supports retain both panels securely in their open positions.

The internal cabinet can be configured with shelves, document holders, and equipment compartments for storing brochures, samples, cables, and accessories. Recessed handles, flush-mounted hardware, and positive-action latches provide safe handling and a clean exterior when closed. Optional castors or adjustable feet allow the stand to be moved easily and levelled on uneven floors.

The structure may be manufactured from lightweight aluminium framing with laminated composite, plywood, or sheet-metal panels. Durable edge protection and wipe-clean finishes make the unit suitable for repeated assembly, transport, and use.

**Key features:**
- Compact, collapsible cabinet configuration  
- Downward-folding hinged front panel  
- Upward-opening top information panel  
- Locking hinges or support stays for controlled operation  
- Concealed, configurable storage compartments  
- Replaceable graphic and information surfaces  
- Integrated transport handles and secure closure latches  
- Optional castors, levelling feet, lighting, and cable management  
- Tool-free deployment and rapid pack-down
